blocks.title: Root Cause Analysis, Threat Hunting, and Forensics exam shortcuts
items: Question asks why incident happened → ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
Identify the underlying failure, not just the symptom.
Example: Compromise traced to an unpatched internet-facing server.
No alert, but analysts proactively search for compromise → THREAT HUNTING
Hunting looks for threats that may have bypassed automated detection.
Example: Analysts search for unusual lateral movement.
Need evidence suitable for investigation → DIGITAL FORENSICS
Use forensic collection, preservation, and analysis procedures.
Example: Create a forensic disk image.
Litigation requires data not be deleted → LEGAL HOLD
Suspend normal deletion or retention actions.
Example: Preserve relevant mailboxes and logs.
Need proof of who handled evidence → CHAIN OF CUSTODY
Document every transfer and custodian.
Example: Evidence log records each person who handled the drive.
Need to copy disk for forensic analysis → ACQUISITION
Collect data in a defensible manner while preserving integrity.
Example: Create a bit-for-bit image.
Need to keep evidence unchanged → PRESERVATION
Protect evidence from alteration or contamination.
Example: Store original media securely and analyze a copy.
Legal team needs electronic records produced → E-DISCOVERY
Collect and process electronically stored information for legal proceedings.
Example: Produce relevant email and file records.
blocks.example: Follow the incident-response order carefully, then distinguish response actions from forensic evidence-handling requirements.

questions.q: After an incident, the team determines that an unpatched internet-facing server was the underlying reason for compromise. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Root cause analysis identifies the underlying reason an incident occurred.

questions.q: Analysts proactively search for lateral movement even though no alert has fired. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Threat hunting proactively searches for hidden compromise that automated controls may have missed.

questions.q: A forensic examiner creates a bit-for-bit image of a suspect drive. Which forensic activity is this?
questions.explanation: Acquisition collects forensic evidence, such as a bit-for-bit disk image.

questions.q: A company must stop normal deletion of relevant emails because of pending litigation. Which requirement is this?
questions.explanation: A legal hold requires potentially relevant information to be preserved.

questions.q: Investigators document every person who handled a seized drive and each transfer between custodians. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Chain of custody records who handled or transferred evidence.

questions.q: Original evidence is stored securely and a write blocker is used so it cannot be altered. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Preservation protects evidence from alteration, contamination, or loss.

questions.q: The legal team requests relevant emails and files for production in a lawsuit. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: E-discovery identifies, collects, processes, and produces electronic information for legal proceedings.

questions.q: A forensic analyst documents methods, evidence, conclusions, and incident findings for stakeholders. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Reporting documents and communicates forensic findings and evidence.
